what_worked: Flagging 305 zero-growth rows as likely untracked data is honest and analytically useful.
fix_next: Deliver on the title's promise: show which categories or companies are actually moving, not just that size doesn't predict growth.
verdict: Narrow, honest four-slide read that never answers its own headline question.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: visible bar values (96+346+51+92 = 585 shown, plus unlabeled bars) don't clearly reconcile with callout totals 344+305+337=986; 14 rows unaccounted for vs n=1000. Minor but sloppy. Slide 3 Spearman ≈ 0.18 is asserted without sourcing; reference Pearson r=0.025 is for a different pair, so unverifiable but not clearly wrong.

evidence.insight: Only real finding is that revenue size and 30-day growth are weakly correlated (Spearman ~0.18) and that 305 flat-growth rows are suspect. No exploration of categories, providers, geography, or audience type—misses most of the dataset's richness.
evidence.narrative: Three-beat arc (split → size≠speed → implication) is coherent but thin. The title 'Who's Actually Moving?' sets up an identification question the deck never answers—no company or category breakdown is provided.
evidence.framing: Dataset size and freeze date stated on slide 1. No audience explicitly named. No mention of missingness (category 27%, country 24%) which directly affects any growth segmentation. No scope/limitations slide.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 2 callouts 344+305+337=986, leaving 14 rows unaccounted from n=1000 with no explanation. The 216 zero-revenue rows likely overlap with the 305 flat-growth group but this is never clarified. Spearman ≈ 0.18 is plausible but unverifiable against reference data. No causal overclaims, which is good.
evidence.visual: Clean palette, readable bar charts, consistent footer. Slide 4 placeholder colored squares are decorative filler. Only two real charts across four slides feels sparse. Adequate but unremarkable.
evidence.ai_slop: Slide 4 three-card layout with decorative squares feels template-generated. Language is generally substantive, not inflated.

change_reason: Reduced insight from 6→5.5 (single finding, no category/provider exploration), narrative from 6.5→6 (title promise undelivered), framing from 5.5→5 (no missingness disclosure, no explicit audience), accuracy from 6→5.5 (bin reconciliation gap unexplained), removed bonus point (nothing beyond rubric expectations in a 4-slide deck with one finding).
